workflowRecommendation: One implementer, tasks in order 1→5, one jj commit per task (fix, tests, docs, ci), one pull request; the real-jj tests (Task 2) pass against Task 1's code without further source changes. Tester repeats the Task 5 Step 2 driver independently, both the fix and the negative control, and adds the merged-branch shape.

implement: legion-worker — shared workspace binding, jj-only commits via `jj split`, bookmark on `@-` before every push, PR body in READY format with `Dispatch: LEGION-70`.
test-driven-development — every task writes its workspace.test.ts case first and watches it fail (Task 1 Step 7 lists the exact expected failures); the fake-runner argv lists are the contract.
verification-before-completion — the E2E driver's op-log quote and its negative control go into the PR body before the handoff; production check after merge per Task 5 Step 3.
test: legion-worker — the tester runs the Task 5 Step 2 driver outside the suite against a scratch remote with real jj (spec acceptance 3), quotes both op logs in the PR's E2E line, and adds the merged-branch shape (push, `git branch -D` on the remote, provision again, `jj bookmark list` prints nothing).
review: legion-worker — verify CI/Threads/E2E against GitHub, one review per round; check every acceptance line against the test inventory table in the plan, and that the fresh path uses `bookmark set … -r @` (acceptance 1 names it) rather than `bookmark create`.

concerns: CI does not run packages/workspace at all today (Tests workflow runs bun test/biome/tsc in packages/daemon only); plan Task 4 adds it — architect may strike it (reported).

Pre-existing jj hazard, out of scope, reported to architect: after a merged PR's branch is deleted, `jj git fetch` abandons the branch's commits even under a live workspace's working copy, rebases that working copy onto the fork point and leaves it stale until the next `jj workspace update-stale` (which removes the files). The old code crashed on this whenever the bookmark was not on `@`; after the fix the provision succeeds and the next provision's update-stale repairs it. `git.abandon-unreachable-commits = false` on the clone would stop it; design decision for a separate issue.

Acceptance-2's literal check (provision, push, delete remote branch, provision again → bookmark list prints nothing) only holds when the pushed commit is still the bookmark's target at fetch time: provisioning leaves `.omp/config.yml` unsnapshotted on `@`, and the next `update-stale` snapshot moves a bookmark that sits on `@`. The planned test snapshots (`jj status`) before pushing; the tester's out-of-suite run must do the same.

A pre-existing local bookmark on a workspace jj does not know (only after a hand-run `jj workspace forget`) is moved forward or refused sideways by the fresh path's `bookmark set -r @`; the spec names `set`, so `create` was not used. Noted, not changed.
verifiedFacts: jj 0.44.0 and 0.45.1: `jj bookmark list legion/<KEY>` prints exactly '' on stdout, exit 0, stderr `Warning: No matching bookmarks for names: …` when absent; one row when present; exact name match (legion/X-1 does not match legion/X-10).
Both binaries: after the remote branch is deleted, `jj git fetch` deletes the tracked local bookmark that still matches it (`bookmark: legion/X@origin [deleted] untracked`).

Both binaries: `jj workspace add --revision <gone bookmark>` prints `Created workspace` then `Error: Revision … doesn't exist` and leaves the workspace registered on the root commit — so the recovery branch must check before adding.
Daemon never reads WorkspaceSpec.bookmark; daemon tests pinning provisioning argv: packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/processes.test.ts:699 and :810 (fresh path).
E2E driver in plan Task 5 Step 2 runs against today's code and prints `point bookmark legion/WIDGETS-42 operations: 2` (negative control verified); a no-op fetch records no op-log entry.
